assertion.text: Erdős Problem #174: declared status 'open'. Formalized: no. A finite set $A\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is called Ramsey if, for any $k\geq 1$, there exists some $d=d(A,k)$ such that in any $k$-colouring of $\mathbb{R}^d$ there exists a monochromatic copy of $A$. Characterise the Ramsey sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Prize: no. Tags: geometry, ramsey theory.
